p.i: DEfinite ô tandem : quid enim indulgetis inani Pallásque, Mársque iurgio?
Ac primum tibi Mars, primum tibi Pallas honore Ambo arrogatis immeriti?
Imò agite, & Diuæ (sic fas expostulat) vni Pallásque, Mársque, cedite.
Definite ô: quid enim studia in contraria vates Caco astuatis impetu?
Palladáque hic Marti, Martem molimine eodem Præponit ille Palladi?
Imò agite, & Diuam sociatis laudibus vnam Præferte Marti, & Palladi.
Artibus Aoniis vincit quæ Pallada, vincit Virtute Martem bellica.
Illa suos longa, quàm longa, pace Britannos, Artésque doctas souerat.
Nec dum alius bello, tot iam labentibus annis, Tantam aufus ire in Principem.
Aggressi innumera vix tandem classe Gigantis Fastum repente contudit.
Mentior? anne ipso dirimi hæc certamina vultis Liuore teste & iudice?
Fare agedum, veræ ad cumulum, argutissime Liuor Ecquid requiris gloriæ?

page.notes: The first word of the poem is a large woodcut-style initial "D" followed by "efinite"; transcribed as "Definite" with the initial joined. The first line's "Defi-nite" is read as "Definite" after the initial, with "Essinite" in the scan. Words with a long-s form were normalised to plain s. Uncertain readings: "Definite" (first line) and "Liuore" (appears clearly). No illegible words. Ornamented catchword/signature absent.
